observations: A roughly circular face fills most of the canvas, ringed by a halo of olive-green lobed shapes studded with yellow and cyan dots that radiate outward as a collar.

The face interior is built from heavy black spiral and loop lines over warm brown-orange tones, with scattered red, green, and pink dots across the cheeks and nose bridge; two white teeth are visible inside a dark-outlined mouth at center-bottom.
The top edge carries a row of dark red upright blade shapes alternating with cyan circles, with a dense tangle of multicolored scribble lines filling the forehead area behind them.
reading: The face pushes outward from the canvas center, its radiating collar of lobed forms and dotted beads giving it the weight of a ceremonial object. Spiral lines wind tightly around each eye socket, pulling the gaze inward even as the visible teeth and scattered bright dots push energy back out. The result reads as both confrontational and festive, two moods held in the same structure.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #101 and #103. Where #101 uses a flat gray ground and open scribble lines with no surrounding ornament, #102 adds a full decorative border, shifting the face from raw sketch toward something closer to an emblem.

connections.reason: Both works share a frontal face-filling structure and layered scribble lines, but #101 strips away all border ornament and uses a cool gray ground, making the contrast in decorative density direct and visible.

From the nnotb owned subset, #172 shares the same dark green background and a toothed mouth at center, allowing a cross-collection comparison of how the same ground color and mouth placement carry different line density and border treatment.

tags: warm-brown face on dark green ground
lookingQuestion: The cyan and yellow dots scattered across the face and those ringing the outer collar share the same colors — do they read as one continuous pattern crossing the boundary between face and frame, or do they stay visually separate?
ambiguities: The lobed border shapes could be read as leaves, petals, or purely abstract forms; no supplied evidence resolves which reading the work supports.
Candidate #103 shows a muted gray-ground face with closed eyes and no border ornament — the contrast is real but less specific than the #101 and nnotb #172 connections, so it was not selected.
